scores.design: Design 3: "Wetter" tab with hour strip and water-clipped sea-state overlay
scores.perCriterion: Totals are on a 0-100 basis: sum of score x weight, divided by 10. Skipper task fit and glanceability (25): 8.2. It is the only design that answers 'when' as numbers, not only by scrubbing: a 3-hourly day strip with wind range, gusts, direction and sea height per column, plus day buttons for jumping between days. Both work with wet fingers (columns at least 48x72, day buttons at least 44). The map answers 'where'. Its weaknesses: the summary is scoped to the viewport, which is a new idea and mixes sheltered and exposed water, and there is no number at the start harbour. Coherence (20): 7. It adds a fifth tab and needs a ui-modernization §6 amendment. Boot already broke that non-goal, so there is precedent. It adds no map chrome, keeps the existing persisted toggle keys, and keeps the hour off the departure field (only the explicit 'Als Abfahrt übernehmen' writes it), which respects the two-clocks rule. Tablet legibility (15): 7. The values sit in the panel and sheet and the map chrome stays as today. At the 1180 wide floor the strip scrolls horizontally (content about 334 px, 8 x 48 px columns). The claimed 'card fits in ~540 px' at 820x1180 is unverified and looks optimistic: summing its own rows with gaps gives roughly 700+ px, so the sheet will likely sit at the 649 px 55vh cap and scroll, and the map stays at about 470 px. State honesty (10): 8.5. It covers loading, refreshing, stale (STALE_THRESHOLD_MS), offline empty and offline held (including the active plan's grids, labelled), typed per-feed errors, partial failures, horizon end, a seed past the horizon, no hours left, and the mask still loading. Overlay interplay (10): 8.5. The overlay is tab-scoped, so two forecast clocks are never on the map at once. The route stays and its own weather is hidden. Anchoring is explicit through an exported anchor list. It needs a structural guard that only one WaveLayer instance exists. Risk and scope (10): 6.5. Default-tab specs keep their start state; the only hard break is layout.spec:848 toHaveCount(4) (verified). It splits into two PRs with a vector-cell fallback as the cut line. The scope is large, though (sparkline, strip, scope summary, ConditionsLayer, tab fit), and adds a third mask-sized texture. Extensibility to #1855 (10): 8. A second card in the same tab shares the departure clock, the held grid and an explicit stack slot. Verified against the code: handleHarborPick (App.tsx ~:1206) has no tab gate; the tablist is automatic activation (App.tsx comment ~:1236), so the 600 ms dwell is genuinely needed; route.windBarbs.timeSlider = 'Vorhersagezeitpunkt' (reused safely only because the RouteLayer cluster unmounts in Wetter); pendingDestinationFocus exists (App.tsx:689); depthColor.ts is NOT_IN_CLOSURE (closure.mjs run). Not verified: the sheet-fit height, raster repaint cost, the ewam horizon and axis start.
scores.fatalFlaws: No fatal flaw. Decisive weaknesses: (1) The fifth tab breaks layout.spec:848 toHaveCount(4) and needs a §6 amendment plus a maintainer ruling on #1854. Label fit at 280/320 px is only nice-to-have. (2) The '~540 px card' claim at 820x1180 is unverified and likely optimistic. If the sheet hits the 55vh cap, the strip (its best glanceability feature) can sit below the fold on the narrow design floor until the sheet is scrolled. (3) Calm versus no-data is cued only by arrows, which fails for a cell with finite Hs and a NaN direction; calm #EDF8FB at 0.45 then reads as nothing. (4) The viewport-scoped min/max summary is a new concept that moves when the user pans, and it has no point value at the start harbour. (5) Where scopePoints gets the narrow sheet height is not specified.

scores.design: Design 2: "Wann zuerst" departure-and-conditions card at the top of the Plan tab
scores.perCriterion: Skipper task fit and glanceability (25): 6.5. 'Hour = departure' is an elegant identity for the when-then-where flow, and the readout at the origin harbour is the number a skipper wants. Costs: peeking at a later hour silently moves the departure; each session needs an explicit 'Wind & Seegang laden' press; there are no day-jump buttons (the day ticks are aria-hidden), so on a 390 px wide panel the slider moves about 1.7 px per hour; on narrow, Start/Ziel are pushed one scroll lower; and the view lives on the Plan tab only. Coherence (20): 8.5. It is the most conservative design: no new tab, no map chrome, one clock, the Card/Field/Slider primitives, persisted toggle keys shared with the cluster (the listener registry in usePersistedToggle.ts:25 is verified, so live sync holds). Tablet legibility (15): 7. Controls are in the panel and sheet, the hour value is 1.25rem/600, and the map is unchanged at about 470 px on narrow. The loaded card is about 330 px (estimated, not measured). State honesty (10): 8.5. It covers idle, loading, ready, stale at 12 h, held grid, offline with nothing held, offline showing the plan's grids, typed failures, beyond horizon (the overlay clears and never clamps to the last hour), expired, and partial. Overlay interplay (10): 7.5. conditionsOnMap gives one forecast on the map and the cluster shows a status line plus 'Routenvorhersage zeigen'. But two time controls can be visible on the Plan tab when a plan exists, and touching the card scrubber both switches the map and dirties the form. Risk and scope (10): 6. Moving #planner-departure into a new first card shifts the default tab's layout for every e2e spec (#1405), retires the #762 narrow-column regime, and splits planner.departureSafetyContext, which PlannerPanel.test.tsx:1880 pins. The raster and RouteLayer override are about the same work as in the other two designs. Re-rendering App on every scrub tick has a fallback specified. Extensibility to #1855 (10): 7.5. It is a natural third block, since origin and departure are already inputs there. Verified: buildUrl() has no departure parameter (openMeteo.ts:55), so the within-TTL same-grid claim holds; planFormDirty exists (App.tsx:72); lib/plan.ts is NOT_IN_CLOSURE and types.ts is IN_CLOSURE (closure.mjs run, matching the design's claim); 7x getByLabel('Abfahrt'), getByText('Legende', {exact:true}) in datalayers.spec, and 2x getByRole('slider', {name:'Vorhersagezeitpunkt'}), so the 'Vorhersagestunde' name is safe. Not verified: the card height, per-tick render cost, and the 1/4-resolution raster quality at z>=10.
scores.fatalFlaws: No fatal flaw. Decisive weaknesses: (1) Coupling scrub to departure. A skipper browsing six days for a window keeps rewriting the routing input. With a plan loaded, every peek makes the form dirty and flips the map to conditions. The issue asks to 'decide' carry-over, and an implicit write is the riskiest answer. (2) It rearranges the busiest panel on the default tab (departure field moved, guidance string split, compact row single-column), which touches the most e2e start states of the three designs. (3) No day-jump control. (4) Conditions are visible only on the Plan tab and only after a manual load each session.

scores.design: Design 1: Forecast dock — "Wind & Seegang" map mode with a bottom time scrubber
scores.perCriterion: Skipper task fit and glanceability (25): 6.5. It is map-first and works from Plan, Routes and Boot. The big readout gives conditions at the Start harbour, and the toggle and close are one control. But on the narrow 820x1180 floor the dock takes about 120 px out of the roughly 470 px of map above a 649 px planner sheet that stays up, leaving about 342 px (about 29% of the screen) for the very thing being judged. There is no day-jump control (drag about 97 px per day, or tap ◀/▶ 24 times). Coherence (20): 6. It respects the tier order and uses primitives, but a floating map panel is close to the 'map-first + floating panel' direction that ui-modernization §1 rejected. It adds a fourth occluder that ScaleBar, the depth-legend gate and both Tier-2 clusters must budget against. Tablet legibility (15): 6. Wide works (704 px dock at the bottom right). Narrow is cramped, and at 1180 wide the dock spans under the top-left stack's column. raster-resampling: 'linear' blends adjacent band colours into tints that are not in the legend. State honesty (10): 9. It is the most thorough: 1 h and 12 h age tiers, stale-while-revalidate, offline held versus none with the plan-grid source labelled, typed errors, partials, a wave-coverage bar for a shorter ewam horizon, and a mask-missing message. Overlay interplay (10): 8. A single owner (RouteLayer override), a note line replacing the cluster's weather toggles and slider, auto-close keyed on plan.id plus createdAtMs, and suspension on Live. Risk and scope (10): 4.5. The chip is always visible, which changes the start state of every spec (#1405) and of 8 map-hit-testing specs. It needs three Tier-2 height budgets plus a ScaleBar occluder, a useSheetHeight extraction from LiveView (the --live-sheet-h writer at LiveView.tsx:372 is per card, not :root), an ODbL topmost hit-test at wide, and the raster. This is the map-chrome layout surface that has the worst regression history in this repo (#208/#368/#909). Extensibility to #1855 (10): 7. A segmented second mode reuses the clock, but a NumberInput, sail-plan chip, progress and cancel crowd a dock of about 120 px. Verified: buildUrl() has no departure parameter; RouteLayer's setup uses installStyleSetup on [map] (RouteLayer.tsx:1250) and the cluster returns null without a plan (:1842); max-height: none at wide (app.css ~:5139/:5182); beaufortForce is private to DepartureCompare.tsx:37; the persisted-toggle listener registry exists. Not verified: the dock height, the attribution clearance, and repaint cost at k=2.
scores.fatalFlaws: No single fatal flaw, but the narrowest margin of the three. Decisive weaknesses: (1) The squeeze on the narrow design floor: about 342 px of map above a 120 px dock and a 649 px sheet that stays up. (2) An always-visible Tier-2 chip changes every spec's start state and adds a participant to the most fragile layout coupling in the app (three same-tier height budgets, the ScaleBar ceiling, the depth-legend gate, ODbL at wide). Missing one gives a same-tier overlap that no z-index can fix. (3) Linear raster resampling produces intermediate colours at band boundaries that are not in the legend. (4) No day-jump control. (5) It reintroduces a floating panel over the map, the shape ui-modernization §1 rejected.

winner: Design 3: "Wetter" tab with hour strip and water-clipped sea-state overlay
graftsFromOthers:
Ideas from Designs 1 and 2 to graft onto Design 3:
(1) A conditions line at the Start harbour, from D1 'Start: Bft 4 aus 225° · Seegang 0,6 m' or D2 conditions.readout.origin. Show it next to D3's viewport range, because a skipper wants the number where they leave, not only a regional span.
(2) A calm-versus-no-data cue that does not rely on arrows. Either D1's sc-wave-dot ring for cells with finite Hs and NaN direction, or D2's canvas-drawn 1-px cell outline on water pixels only.
(3) Nearest resampling, which D2 also chose and D3 already uses. Explicitly reject D1's 'linear', which blends band colours.
(4) D1's wave-coverage bar under the slider: solid where the wave axis has data, empty past the ewam horizon. The ewam horizon is unverified and may be shorter than the wind horizon.
(5) D1's lib/useSheetHeight.ts extraction, writing --sc-sheet-h. D3's scopePoints needs the narrow sheet height to exclude the sheet band and never says where it comes from.
(6) A narrow-layout order that keeps the glanceable part above the fold, since the ~540 px card claim is likely optimistic. Put header, steppers and day strip first. Put the summary into a slimmer single line or the slider's valuetext. Collapse toggles and legend into one Disclosure.
(7) D2's conditions.legend.cells honesty line ('each shaded block is one model cell of about 11 × 6 km; coarse at coasts and in narrow fjords').
(8) D2's rAF/draft-index fallback, in case per-tick App re-renders while scrubbing are janky on a tablet.
(9) D1's fresh/stale age tiers: plain age line under 1 h, age chip from 1 h, warning wash from 12 h. Also D1's refetch on the 'online' event while the tab is open, with no timers.
(10) D1's barb halo underlay in windBarbs.ts, for daylight legibility over the purple bands and the depth hatch. This is image-only; the Okabe-Ito ink is unchanged.
(11) D1's e2e rendering proof by sampling screenshot pixels at a known land point and a known water point, with a positive control. Needed because jsdom's getContext returns null.
(12) Design 2's verified fact that buildUrl() has no departure parameter: a plan started within the 10-min TTL reuses the exact grid the skipper judged. Say this in D3's handoff copy or status line.

scores.design: Design 1: Forecast dock ("Wind & Seegang" map mode with bottom time scrubber)
scores.perCriterion: Task fit/glanceability 8/10 (x25=200): a map mode reached by one labelled chip, with the hour scrubber next to the thumb at narrow and the map content directly above it. A text readout at Start (Bft, direction, Hs) gives the at-a-glance answer. The browse hour is kept separate from departure and handed over only by an explicit 'Als Abfahrt übernehmen', which answers the issue's carry-over question. Verified: harbour taps work on any tab (App.tsx handleHarborPick -> resolveHarborPickTarget(null, hasOrigin) gives origin-if-empty, else destination, with no tab gate), so the 'tap a harbour mid-browse' handoff is real. Verified: buildUrl() has no departure parameter, so a plan made within GRID_CACHE_TTL_MS reuses the grid. Cost: at 820x1180 the open dock takes about 120 px of the ~470 px of map above the sheet, leaving ~342 px. Coherence 6.5/10 (x20=130): §1 of ui-modernization rejected Map-first because it was the 'largest rework and most risk to the shipped layouts'. A mode-scoped Tier-2 map control is not that shell restructure and is a sibling of the existing .route-layer-controls cluster, so it keeps both §1 and §6. It places by tier with no new z-index and uses the primitives. It does add a third time-control location and a third legend location, and it adds a large 704 px floating box at wide. Verified: Slider has no aria-label prop, so the sr-only label is correct. LiveView's --live-sheet-h is set on the card element and only on narrow, not on :root, so the --sc-sheet-h extraction is new work, not a reuse. Legibility 7/10 (x15=105): solid --sc-bg, 1.25rem tabular readout, 44 px everywhere, a 44 px slider rule, and halo barbs. Wide is comfortable. Narrow is tight at 342 px of map. State honesty 9/10 (x10=90): the most complete state set: loading, refresh-with-held, age tiers that reuse STALE_THRESHOLD_MS, offline none/held including the displayed plan's in-memory grids, typed errors via the hoisted mapWindError, both partials, the wind horizon, a wave-coverage bar for an unverified ewam horizon, mask missing, and a source/authority line. It correctly notes that the cache refetches after the TTL and yields nothing on failure (verified in createGridCache). Overlay 8/10 (x10=80): a single WaveLayer owner (RouteLayer). With a plan, the plan weather is replaced and the duplicate toggles and slider are hidden, so one clock is on screen. It closes on a plan-id+createdAtMs change, applying the CLAUDE.md remount lesson, and is suspended on Live. The water-clipped raster keeps the §0 centre-cull, and markers separate calm from no-data. Risk 5/10 (x10=50): it adds a participant to three same-tier height budgets (route cluster, .map-stack-tl at wide where both are max-height:none today, verified in app.css ~:5208, and depthLegendGate) plus a ScaleBar occluder. That is exactly the coupling class CLAUDE.md shows regressing (#374/#382/#909/#1606). It also adds an always-visible chip (#1405), which shifts every spec's map click points, an ODbL attribution hit-test obligation, and a raster. Its estimate is 4-5 days. Extensibility 7/10 (x10=70): a segmented [Wind & Seegang | Reichweite] dock with the scrubber as the departure input is coherent, but duration, sail plan, compute, progress and cancel on a map dock will crowd at narrow.
scores.fatalFlaws: None fatal. Near-fatal: the open dock adds a new Tier-2 participant to three hand-maintained same-tier height budgets (.route-layer-controls, .map-stack-tl at wide, depthLegendGate) and to ScaleBar's runtime occluder set. Miss one and you get a Tier-2/Tier-2 overlap that no z-index may fix, the regression class this repo has repeatedly shipped and re-fixed. The narrow map shrinks to ~342 px while the dock is open. The --sc-sheet-h variable is new; LiveView's --live-sheet-h is not on :root today.

scores.design: Design 2: "Wann zuerst": departure-and-conditions card at the top of the Plan tab
scores.perCriterion: Task fit/glanceability 6/10 (x25=150): the card sits directly under the map at narrow with a readout at origin, and the map stays unobstructed. It pays twice for that. (a) Primary-flow pushdown at the design floor, measured against a-coldload-noplan-plan-820x1180: today the Start combobox is at ~y740, Ziel at ~y895 and the sticky 'Route planen' bar starts at ~y1090. An idle card of ~200 px (title, moved Abfahrt field, intro, button) above Reise puts Start at ~y940 and Ziel at ~y1095, under the sticky bar, on every Plan-tab cold load whether or not the skipper ever loads a forecast. Loaded (~330 px, the design's own estimate) Reise starts at ~y930 and Ziel is off-screen. (b) Hour equals departure: every scrub writes a routing input. With a plan loaded, peeking at Sunday dirties the form (planFormDirty exists in lib/planForm.ts) for a Sunday departure, so 'browse' and 'decide' are the same gesture. The issue framed carry-over as a decision; this design decides 'identity', and a maintainer asking for proper UX will ask what that costs. Coherence 7/10 (x20=140): no map chrome, the tier order is untouched, primitives are used, and persisted toggles are shared. Verified: usePersistedToggle's listenersByKey registry syncs instances live. But it changes the Plan card's own IA: it moves the departure field, splits planner.departureSafetyContext, makes .planner-compact-row single-column, and puts a second slider on the Plan tab when a plan exists. Name choices hold against e2e. Verified: datalayers.spec uses getByText('Legende', {exact:true}); compass.spec scopes its non-exact match to the cluster; getByLabel('Abfahrt') appears 7x across 5 files, and the id and label are kept. Legibility 7.5/10 (x15=112.5): the map is clear in both branches and the 1.25rem value reads well. In the 390 px wide panel the track gives ~2 px per hour, which the steppers mitigate. State honesty 8.5/10 (x10=85): thorough. It covers idle (no fetch, keeping the zero-request guards true), loading, stale at 12 h, offline none/held/plan-grid, typed errors, beyond horizon, expired, partial and mask. Its closure claim checks out: closure.mjs files at 7a08b939 gives lib/plan.ts NOT_IN_CLOSURE and types.ts IN_CLOSURE. Overlay 7/10 (x10=70): one forecast drives the map at a time, but the conditionsOnMap state machine flips on any user Abfahrt edit. Editing departure to re-plan therefore swaps the map to the area forecast, which needs a user-versus-programmatic write split. Its 1/4-resolution nearest raster with in-canvas cell outlines is the best calm-versus-no-data cue of the three. Risk 6.5/10 (x10=65): no map-chrome couplings. The costs are the PlannerPanel restructure (layout.spec #762 regime lost, PlannerPanel tests), every spec's panel positions shifting, the raster, and the departure-write wrapper. Extensibility 7.5/10 (x10=75): a third card block for #1855 has panel room and already holds origin and departure.
scores.fatalFlaws: None fatal. Near-fatal: (1) it pushes Start/Ziel below the sticky action bar on every Plan-tab session at the 820 px design floor, a permanent regression to the primary task paid even by users who never open the forecast; (2) browsing the forecast is a write to a routing input, so peeking with a plan loaded dirties the form and loses a deliberately typed departure.

scores.design: Design 3: "Wetter" tab with hour strip and water-clipped sea-state overlay
scores.perCriterion: Task fit/glanceability 7.5/10 (x25=187.5): the 3-hourly day strip plus the 6-day sparkline is the only glance-level 'when' comparison any design offers, and it is strong for judging conditions first. The browse hour is decoupled and carried over explicitly to Plan, with Ziel focused via the pendingDestinationFocus path, which exists in App.tsx. Verified: harbour taps work on this tab. Its weakness is the 'where' answer: the summary is a min/max over the visible viewport ('im Kartenausschnitt'). That number changes with pan and zoom, can be dominated by open sea far from the skipper's harbour, and there is no point readout at Start, only the popup. Coherence 5.5/10 (x20=110): it is a new IA change. ui-modernization §6 says 'No new IA (tabs stay Plan / Routes / Live)'. The Boot tab already made that list stale, but §6 still owes an amendment. It also adds conditionsActive mode switches to both RouteLayer and DataLayers, so the hatch and contour rows move between components on that tab, and it needs a structural guard against two WaveLayer instances that share source ids. Legend in the card and no map chrome are good. Legibility 7/10 (x15=105): the map is unobstructed, strip columns are at least 48x72 px, and stepper and day targets are 44 px. Its claim that the narrow card fits ~540 px (giving ~580 px of map) is the design's claim, not a measurement. Summing its own rows against its stated 44/48/72 px minimums gives over 600 px before gaps, so it likely hits the 55vh cap (649 px) and scrolls, leaving the same ~470 px of map as today. At 390 px wide the strip scrolls horizontally. State honesty 8/10 (x10=80): thorough, including a 600 ms dwell before fetching and a seed-clamped horizon note. 'Wetter' as a tab name leans toward reading as a weather service, which the disclaimer has to counter. Overlay 7.5/10 (x10=75): clean. The route stays and plan weather is hidden on the tab, so there is one clock. Anchoring is explicit. The cost is that map semantics now depend on the tab. Risk 4/10 (x10=40): the largest scope, two PRs at ~4.5 days by its own estimate, which is tight for one release. It means a fifth tab (#299's toHaveCount(4) in layout.spec:848, plus tab-order and keyboard specs across ~24 files using role 'tab'), DataLayers and RouteLayer mode props, the area-summary engine, strip, sparkline, and a new camera call site that needs an allowlist entry. Its one strength here is a clean cut line: PR A, the land-tint raster, ships independently. Extensibility 8/10 (x10=80): a second card in the same tab, a held grid usable offline, and an explicit layer slot. The tab name strains for 'reachable area'.
scores.fatalFlaws: None fatal. Near-fatal: it contradicts ui-modernization §6's tab IA and needs an amendment on top of the waves §0 amendment all three need, and its two-PR scope exceeds the release by its own estimate. The area-range summary is a viewport statistic that moves with pan and zoom, so it is a weak 'conditions at my harbour' answer.

winner: Design 1: Forecast dock ("Wind & Seegang" map mode). D1 and D2 are within rounding (7.25 vs 6.98), so the tie is broken by the consistency criterion I judge on. D1 is the only design that leaves the existing information architecture intact: the planner card order, the tab set and the panel are all untouched. Its cost when off is one 44 px chip, and when on it is a reversible map mode. D2 pays its cost in the primary task itself: at the 820 px design floor, Ziel moves under the sticky 'Route planen' bar on every Plan-tab session, and every forecast peek writes a routing input. D3 changes the tab IA (§6). D1's own cost is engineering coupling (three same-tier height budgets plus a ScaleBar occluder), which named e2e guards can bound. The other two designs' costs are user-facing regressions or IA changes that a test cannot bound. Under ui-modernization §1, the Map-first rejection rested on 'largest rework and most risk to the shipped layouts'. A mode-scoped Tier-2 map control is a sibling of the existing .route-layer-controls cluster, not that restructure. This ranking holds under a ±0.5 change to any single criterion except a large cut to D1's task-fit score.
graftsFromOthers:
Graft onto D1. From D3:
(1) The delivery split: ship the water-clipped wave raster (the land-tint fix, which also improves plan mode and the README hero) as its own PR A first, with the vector-cell fallback (lower opacity plus an arrow-marks-data legend line) as the cut line if it slips. This lowers D1's biggest scope risk.
(2) The glance-level 'when' comparison, which only D3 offers: a compact 3-hourly strip or 6-day wind sparkline with a sea-band ribbon. At wide put it above the dock's slider; at narrow put it inside the upward legend panel so it does not grow the dock band.
(3) The speed-weighted circular-mean direction with 'umlaufend'/'variable' below a resultant of 0.5, for the Start readout and popup.
(4) The conditions.horizon.seedClamped copy and its rule ('Abfahrt {time} liegt außerhalb der Vorhersage; gezeigt wird {shown}').
(5) Strip-column and readout accessible names built from visible text plus sr-only unit words, which satisfies WCAG 2.5.3 without aria-label overrides.
(6) The half-resolution raster row map subsampled from depthCanvasRowMap, with a twin test on its corners, never re-derived.
(7) Exporting the forecast barb layer into waveBeforeId()'s anchor list, so stacking stays explicit whichever layer mounts first.

From D2:
(8) The in-canvas 1-px cell outline on water pixels only, where the nearest lattice index changes. It separates calm from no-data without an edge layer over land and complements D1's per-cell arrow/dot markers.
(9) A shared WindBarbKey component built from barbSegments(), used by both the dock legend and RouteLegend, which today has no barb key.
(10) The conditions.legend.cells copy (each block is one ~11 × 6 km model cell, coarse at coasts and narrow fjords), to disclose resolution honestly.
(11) In-session adoption: once the user has opened the mode, a newer grid fetched by a plan run replaces the held one, so the dock always shows the newest known forecast. Nothing is adopted before a user action, so the zero-Open-Meteo e2e guards stay true.
(12) An explicit no-fetch idle state, already implied by D1's default-off chip; keep the 'Vorhersage laden' wording consistent with D2's offline copy, which separates role=status from role=alert.

Do NOT graft D2's hour=departure identity or its Plan-card restructure. Do NOT graft D3's fifth tab or its viewport min/max summary as the primary readout; keep D1's Start-point readout.

Fix within D1 itself:
- Specify --sc-sheet-h as new :root plumbing. LiveView currently writes --live-sheet-h on the card element, narrow only.
- Consider a one-row dock at narrow (readout plus slider, with the steppers and carry-over in an overflow row) to recover map height from ~342 px.

scores.design: Design 3: "Wetter" tab: a conditions surface with an hour strip and a water-clipped sea-state overlay
scores.perCriterion:
Skipper task fit 8/25w: it is the only design with a week-at-a-glance view (6-day sparkline with wind bars and a sea-band ribbon, day buttons, a 3-hourly numeric strip, an area summary), so you can pick a window without scrubbing hour by hour. The cost is coexistence with the planner: on the Wetter tab the planner panel is hidden, so each judge, pick, plan loop costs a tab switch (Wetter, then Als Abfahrt übernehmen, then Planen, then the link back). Harbour taps still set Start/Ziel on any tab (verified: App.tsx handleHarborPick has no tab gate) and the endpoints line confirms the pick, which partly makes up for it.

Coherence 7/20w: card content in the panel matches the Routes and Boot tabs. It needs an amendment to ui-modernization §6, but Boot is a precedent. It adds a second barb source and layer (sc-conditions-wind-barbs) that duplicates RouteLayer's. The WaveLayer owner swap works mechanically: verified, WaveLayer empties its layers on unmount but keeps them, and setup re-bumps the epoch.

Tablet legibility 7/15w: its claim that the narrow sheet is about 540 px with about 580 px of map is wrong by its own row list. Header 44, summary ~52, sparkline+slider+labels ~96, day buttons 52, strip ≥80, endpoints, actions 52, status, toggles 52, legend 56, padding and the 45 px tab strip sum to about 657 px, above the 649 px cap. So the map stays at about 470 px as today, and the toggles and legend fall below the fold. At 1180x820 (a design-floor tablet) the 3-hourly strip, its main comparison widget, scrolls horizontally inside the 390 px panel. Text is at least 1rem tabular-nums and targets are 44 px or larger.

State honesty 8.5/10w: covers SWR refresh, 12 h stale, offline with nothing held and with something held (including the plan's grids), typed per-feed errors, a per-hour wave gap, the horizon end, a seed clamp, and model names. The weak spot is that the fetch is automatic after a 600 ms tab dwell.

Overlay interplay 8/10w: overlays are exclusive per tab, so only one forecast clock is ever on the map. The route line stays and the RouteLayer weather is hidden. Layer anchoring is explicit.

Risk and scope 6/10w: splitting into PR A (raster) and PR B with a vector fallback is the best risk control of the three. Against that: the 5th tab touches #299 toHaveCount(4) (verified at layout.spec.ts:848), keyboard tab cycling, and DataLayers conditionsActive. It adds a new ConditionsLayer, a duplicate barb layer, and a new fitBounds call site (allowlist).

#1855 fit 8/10w: a second card in the same tab, with an explicit stack slot, the shared hour, and offline use on a held grid. The cleanest home of the three.
scores.fatalFlaws:
None fatal. Most serious:
(1) Wind and waves are fetched IN PARALLEL. This contradicts the verified usePlanFlow ordering: the wave fetch starts after wind resolves, to avoid adding to a wind 429 (usePlanFlow.ts ~:443). This machine has a 429 history on the shared IP. A one-line fix.
(2) The narrow-sheet budget is miscounted: the card hits the 55vh cap, so it gains no map area.
(3) Factual error: 'a profile that has never planned has no barb images yet' is false. RouteLayer is always mounted (App.tsx:1738) and registers the images in setupLayers (RouteLayer.tsx:622). Harmless.
(4) The legend line 'an arrow marks a cell with data' is false for cells with finite Hs and NaN direction.
(5) The ~2.4 MP half-res raster index map must be module-cached per mask, or it is rebuilt on every Wetter entry when the ConditionsLayer/RouteLayer WaveLayer owner swaps.
(6) Shared by all three designs: the hour is hoisted into App state (conditionsHourMs). Every slider tick then re-renders the whole App tree on a tablet, where today the slider is RouteLayer-local (setHourIdx).

scores.design: Design 2: "Wann zuerst" (When first): a departure-and-conditions step at the top of the Plan tab
scores.perCriterion:
Skipper task fit 6.5/25w: the when, then where, then plan flow is natural, and making the hour identical to the departure means the route is planned on the very grid that was judged (verified: buildUrl has no departure parameter and the cache is shared with usePlanFlow's default fetch). But because of that same identity you cannot look at conditions at the ETA, or at any hour other than the one you leave, without changing the routing input. With a plan loaded, every peek dirties the form and swaps the map. There is no multi-day overview beyond day ticks, and an explicit Load click is needed first.

Coherence 7/20w: no new tab, no new map chrome, and it is built from Card, Field and Slider. But it moves the departure Field out of .planner-compact-row, splits planner.departureSafetyContext, and puts a second slider on the Plan tab next to the route cluster's.

Tablet legibility 7.5/15w: the narrow map keeps its ~470 px with no chrome added, and the scrubber sits just under the tab strip. The 1.25rem value and the swatch strip with names are readable. But Start/Ziel move about one scroll lower (Reise at ~y930) for every user, every session.

State honesty 8.5/10w: idle (inert, zero network), loading, stale at 12 h, expired, offline with nothing held (plus a 'show the loaded route's forecast' button), held, typed errors with retry, horizon, partial, and the mask-loading case.

Overlay interplay 7/10w: one forecast at a time via mapForecast, shared persisted toggle keys (verified that usePersistedToggle syncs listeners across instances per key), and a status line plus switch-back button in the route cluster. The rules for flipping conditionsOnMap (user vs programmatic departure writes) are subtle. It does use a wrapper callback rather than a prop-diff, which is right per the #695 lesson.

Risk and scope 6.5/10w: no map-chrome geometry and fetches are explicit only, so the e2e zero-request guards are safe. Its quarter-resolution raster with nearest resampling is the cheapest (~590K px, ~2.4 MB) and the only design to name a draft-index mitigation for per-tick re-render. Against that, the PlannerPanel restructure hits PlannerPanel tests and layout.spec #762. The in-canvas 1-px outlines become 4-16 screen px at z10-z12, and the coast clipping is a blocky 185 m.

#1855 fit 6.5/10w: it fits as a third block in the card, but the card grows further and pushes the planner down again.
scores.fatalFlaws:
None fatal. Most serious, and the largest single task-fit cost across all three designs: scrubbing IS editing the departure. A skipper cannot inspect conditions at arrival time, or browse tomorrow while keeping today's departure, without overwriting a routing input. With a plan shown, each peek also marks the plan form dirty and swaps the map.
Secondary: relocating the departure field taxes the core planning flow even for users who never open the forecast. Outlines drawn on all water pixels do not by themselves separate calm from no-data. The App re-renders on every slider tick (shared with the others); this design at least names a draft-index fallback.

scores.design: Design 1: Forecast dock: a "Wind & Seegang" map mode with a bottom time scrubber
scores.perCriterion:
Skipper task fit 7/25w: one tap on any tab, browsing directly on the map, a readout at the Start harbour (Bft, heading, Hs), a coverage bar for the wave horizon, and an explicit 'Als Abfahrt übernehmen' that keeps the two clocks separate. There is no multi-day overview, so judging a window means scrubbing hour by hour.

Coherence 6/20w: the single rendering owner (a RouteLayer forecast override; verified that the barb layer setup in installStyleSetup is keyed on [map] and that the barb effect only clears on !plan) is the cleanest code shape of the three. But a floating bottom dock over the map edges toward the 'map-first, floating panel' direction that ui-modernization §1 rejected. Its linear raster-resampling blends band colours, so on-screen colours appear that are not in the legend.

Tablet legibility 6/15w: on wide it is fine (a 704 px dock). On narrow the dock takes ~120-148 px out of the ~470 px of visible map in the layout the spec calls the primary cockpit-portrait mode, leaving ~320-340 px. The screenshot at 820x1180 shows how cramped that map already is.

State honesty 9/10w: the most complete. SWR, an age chip from 1 h, a warning at 12 h, offline with nothing held and with something held (session plus displayed plan), typed errors, partial results both ways, a wave-coverage gap, departure beyond the horizon, mask missing. Default-off and unpersisted, so the zero-request e2e guards hold.

Overlay interplay 8/10w: a single owner, the RouteLegend sea block hidden while active, auto-close on a `${plan.id}-${plan.createdAtMs}` change, a dot marker for NaN direction, and a halo on the barbs.

Risk and scope 4/10w: highest of the three. It adds a new Tier-2 participant that forces new bounds on .route-layer-controls, .map-stack-tl at wide, and the depthLegendGate budget. It also adds a ScaleBar occluder, a --sc-sheet-h extraction from LiveView, and an ODbL attribution hit-test. Each of those surfaces has a regression history in this repo (#208, #368, #702, #771, #909, #1606). On top of that, an always-visible chip on Plan/Routes/Boot changes every spec's starting state (#1405), and hit-test click points must be audited across about 8 specs at every viewport.

#1855 fit 6.5/10w: a segmented control in the dock with a shared scrubber is coherent. But duration, sail chip, compute, progress and cancel would crowd a dock that is already about 120 px tall on narrow.
scores.fatalFlaws:
None fatal. Most serious:
(1) Map-chrome geometry risk and the #1405 start-state shift from an always-visible chip. This is the widest e2e blast radius of the three.
(2) In the narrow branch the dock removes roughly a quarter to a third of the already small visible map.
(3) linear resampling renders inter-band colours that are not in the legend.
(4) Shared: forecastTMs in App state re-renders the whole App tree on every slider tick, and no mitigation is named.

winner: Design 3: "Wetter" tab: a conditions surface with an hour strip and a water-clipped sea-state overlay
graftsFromOthers:
Graft onto Design 3:

From Design 1:
- (a) Single rendering owner. Do not build a ConditionsLayer with a duplicate sc-conditions-wind-barbs source and layer, and do not swap WaveLayer owners. Give RouteLayer a `forecast` override ({wind, wave, tMs}) and mount WaveLayer ahead of its `if (!plan) return null`, so App passes the Wetter forecast while that tab is active. Barbs keep the one sc-wind-barbs layer, and layerOrder and the WAVE_STACK_BOTTOM_LAYER anchoring stay unchanged.
- (b) An sc-wave-dot centre marker for cells with finite Hs but NaN direction, so the legend line 'a marker means data' is true everywhere.
- (c) A wave-coverage bar under the scrubber. It shows where the ewam axis ends before the wind horizon, since `waveHourIndexAt` returns null there.
- (d) A conditions-at-Start readout line: Bft from a hoisted `lib/beaufort.ts`, `formatHeading`, and Hs at the planner's origin. It is the keyboard and screen-reader path to the values, and a glance answer for the departure harbour.
- (e) The accessible-name discipline (e.g. 'Seegangsskala…'). Avoid names that are substrings of, or contain, 'Legende', 'Seegang anzeigen', 'Vorhersagezeitpunkt', 'Wassertiefen' or 'Abfahrt', in both de and en.
- (f) The tap-hint legend line, plus the authority/source line with grid.model and the fetch time.
- (g) Optionally, the HALO underlay on the barb images for daylight legibility. This changes plan-mode rendering too, so verify it in a real browser.

From Design 2:
- (h) Sequential fetch: wind first, waves after wind resolves. This mirrors usePlanFlow's 429 caution and replaces Design 3's parallel fetch. Also consider replacing the 600 ms dwell auto-fetch with an explicit 'Wind & Seegang laden' button on first entry. That keeps the zero-request guarantee structural rather than timing-based.
- (i) Keep `raster-resampling: 'nearest'`. Treat Design 2's quarter-resolution canvas (~590K px, ~2.4 MB) as the fallback if one half-resolution repaint plus texture upload exceeds a frame on a mid-range tablet. Measure once on the main thread, where CDP throttling works.
- (j) One shared `nearestCell()` used by both the raster painter and the tap popup, so the popup always matches the tapped block.
- (k) A unit test that the water-clipped partition equals today's ±0.05° rectangles minus land. Include a positive control: a coastal water point whose rectangle covers land pixels must map to -1.
- (l) An offline button to show the loaded route's forecast, and automatic adoption of a newer in-session plan grid once something is held.
- (m) A draft-index scrub commit: label and overlay follow a local draft, and the hour is committed on pointerup/keyup or after 150 ms idle. Better, keep the hour in a small store or ref read by the override, so a slider tick does not re-render the whole App tree. All three designs currently hoist the hour into App state.

Fixes to Design 3 itself:
- Re-budget the narrow card. It currently sums to about 657 px, over the 649 px 55vh cap. Collapse the strip or the toggles behind the legend Disclosure at narrow, and stop claiming map area it does not gain.
- At 1180x820, consider a 6-column strip (00–15 local, next page) instead of horizontal scroll.
- Module-cache the raster index map per mask.
